clue.text: Comment on whisky with enthusiasm!

parts.note: a cheer of encouragement read literally as a remark identifying a glass of Scotch as a distilled drink

explanation.surface: Someone praises a dram of whisky with gusto.
explanation.walkthrough: The everyday cry urging someone on doubles as a literal remark about a drink, since whisky is a spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a stock exclamation of approval for someone's keenness, and literally labels a spirit such as whisky.

clue.text: No lightweight thug

explanation.surface: A heavyweight bruiser is described.
explanation.definitionFit: Something weighty is the opposite of light, and a hired tough or bouncer is slang for a heavy.

clue.text: Award for quiet hopi tal in city of Paris

indicators.note: in tells us the quiet and hospital letters sit within the city

parts.note: Paris, prince of Troy in Greek legend, so his city is Troy
P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
H is the standard abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A prize is given to a peaceful hospital in the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'city of Paris' suggests France, but it means the city of the Trojan prince Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: A cup or shield given to a winner is a prize of this kind.

clue.text: Vagrant with no job becomes a bouncer

parts.note: a vagrant is a tramp, a homeless wanderer
O is the figure zero, meaning none
a line, as in line of work, is a job

explanation.surface: An unemployed tramp turns into a nightclub doorman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bouncer' suggests a club doorman, but here it is something that makes people bounce.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprung canvas frame that gymnasts jump on is something that bounces people.

clue.text: Avon is Paradise

explanation.surface: A river or county is called heaven itself.
explanation.walkthrough: Anthony Eden, British Prime Minister in the 1950s, became Earl of Avon, so the title Avon names him.
explanation.definitionFit: The Earl of Avon was the title given to that Prime Minister, and the Bible's garden of Adam and Eve is a byword for paradise.

clue.text: Bill acquires new back door

parts.note: a bill is a printed notice stuck on a wall, a poster

explanation.surface: Someone named Bill gets a new rear entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name, but it is a placard.
explanation.definitionFit: A small rear or side gate, especially in a castle wall, is a back door.

clue.text: Gardener resolved to retain old instrument

indicators.note: to retain means to keep inside, so one piece is held within the other
resolved in the sense of broken down and reworked, signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener is determined to keep an antique musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolved' rearranges GARDENER into REEDRGAN, and 'to retain' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A harmonium-like keyboard sounding through vibrating metal tongues is a musical instrument.

clue.text: Forming affection for items whilst dismantling them

parts.note: forming affection for someone is taking to them
items are pieces, individual things

explanation.surface: Someone grows fond of objects even while breaking them apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Separating something into its parts is the idiom for dismantling it.

clue.text: Silly bairn feared the upheaval

indicators.note: an upheaval is a violent disturbance, signalling these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A frightened Scottish child is upset by the commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: A bairn is a Scottish word for a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone silly and scatterbrained is described with this idiom for a light head.

clue.text: To add detail is complicated

explanation.surface: Expanding on something makes it intricate.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means expand on a point; as an adjective it means intricate and detailed.

clue.text: Small vegetable of glossy appearance

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a leek is an onion-family vegetable

explanation.surface: A little vegetable looks shiny.
explanation.definitionFit: Smooth and shiny hair or fur is described as glossy.

clue.text: Retail outlet delivers trifles before dance

indicators.note: before places the trifles piece ahead of the dance piece

parts.note: trifles are toys, things of little value
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: A shop sends out cheap goods ahead of a ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trifles' suggests puddings, but here it means playthings.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop selling children's playthings is a retail outlet.

clue.text: Drug a valiant man at home

parts.note: a brave man is a hero
in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: A brave man at home takes a narcotic.
explanation.definitionFit: An addictive opiate made from morphine is a drug.

clue.text: Renunciation by mariner, say, in the country

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for say inside the country

parts.note: a nation is a country
EG, for example, means say

explanation.surface: A sailor living abroad gives something up.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-denial, giving up something wanted, is renunciation.

clue.text: English mother acquires cheese

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal

explanation.surface: An English mum buys some cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: A mild Dutch cheese with a red wax rind is one such variety.

clue.text: Mishaps occur when accountant is full of depression

parts.note: ACC is a short form linked with accounts and accountancy

indicators.note: full of means the word is holds the depression within it

parts.note: taken as written
a dent is a hollow, a depression

explanation.surface: Things go wrong when the bookkeeper is gloomy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depression' suggests low spirits, but it is a physical hollow.
explanation.definitionFit: Unplanned harmful events are mishaps.

clue.text: Absconding debtor urged to avoid daytime air travel

definitions.text: urged to avoid daytime air travel

explanation.surface: A debtor on the run is told not to take day flights.
explanation.definitionFit: A disreputable person who flees debts is a shady sort, and literally the phrase advises flying in darkness.

clue.text: Labourer framed by sponsor offering bribe

indicators.note: framed by means surrounded, so the worker sits within the sponsor

parts.note: a backer is a financial sponsor
a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: A worker is set up by a sponsor who offers a bung.
explanation.walkthrough: 'framed' suggests a false accusation, but it means enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret payment slipped to someone under the counter is a bribe.

clue.text: Liquor left in a glass trodden underfoot

explanation.surface: Leftover drink in a glass gets stamped on.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the dregs left in a drinking glass, and also a layer of leather in the heel of a shoe that is walked on.

clue.text: Break utensils on the way back

indicators.note: on the way back means the word for utensils is read in reverse

parts.note: pans are cooking utensils

explanation.surface: Kitchenware gets broken on the return journey.
explanation.definitionFit: To crack or fracture suddenly is to break.

clue.text: Discarded goods taken from planes in the morning

parts.note: jets are aircraft
AM, ante meridiem, means in the morning

explanation.surface: Cargo is dumped from aircraft at dawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Cargo thrown overboard to lighten a ship, later washed ashore, is discarded goods.

clue.text: He is warned to reform

indicators.note: to reform means to form again in a new shape, signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man is cautioned to mend his ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' is the whole definition: a man's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: A male given name, borne by Scotland's patron saint, names a man.

clue.text: Ordinary greeting delivered with fury

parts.note: ave is Latin for hail, a greeting
rage is fury

explanation.surface: A normal hello is delivered angrily.
explanation.definitionFit: Typical or middling is ordinary.

clue.text: Decorate seamen after a party

indicators.note: after places the seamen piece behind the party

parts.note: a do is an informal party
RN, the Royal Navy, stands for seamen

explanation.surface: Sailors put up decorations after a party.
explanation.definitionFit: To embellish or beautify is to decorate.

clue.text: Boss employs retiring ex-pupil after some hesitation

indicators.note: after places the former pupil piece behind the hesitation

parts.note: um is the sound of hesitation

indicators.note: retiring means going backwards, so the letters for ex-pupil are reversed

parts.note: OB, old boy, is a former pupil

explanation.surface: A manager hires a former student who hesitates and then retires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' suggests an employer, but it is a raised knob, as on a shield.
explanation.definitionFit: The central raised knob on a shield is a boss.

clue.text: Group explains why the trawlermen can't fish

definitions.text: explains why the trawlermen can't fish

explanation.surface: A crew explains why the fishermen cannot work.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of nine musicians is a group, and read as two words it says the fishing crew lacks netting.

clue.text: Where Kentish lasses have style?

parts.note: read in two parts, girls plus a manner or quality, naming the place in Kent where they live

explanation.surface: A question about where the fashionable girls of Kent live.
explanation.walkthrough: The county town of Kent splits into a word for young women and a word for style.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the county town of Kent, so a natural home for Kentish girls.

clue.text: A hellish date was not a success?

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld and a name for hell itself
a date is an appointment

explanation.surface: A dreadful evening out was a flop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'date' suggests a romance, but it is a fixed meeting time, and Dis is the classical underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that falls short of hopes is a letdown, not a success.
